cards.a: Austria - bus stop sign
cards.note:
Austrian bus stop signs contain a yellow and green circle with the letter H.

NOTE: This design is relatively unique in Europe. The only other country with similar bus stop signs is Germany.

cards.a: Belgium  - Flanders and Brussels bus stop signs
cards.note: Bus stop signs in Flanders (and Brussels) have a white rectangle at the top. In Wallonia they will have a yellow top.

cards.a: Belgium  - Wallonia bus stop sign
cards.note: Bus stop signs in Flanders (and Brussels) have a white rectangle at the top. In Wallonia they will have a yellow top.

cards.a: Estonia - bus stop sign
cards.note:
Estonian bus stop signs have this design.

The bus has four windows. This is mostly useful to distinguish it from the Latvian bus stop sign, which has five windows.

Note, however, that Lithuania has the same bus stop signs as Estonia.

cards.a: Finland - bus stop sign
cards.note:
Finland has two styles of bus stop signs, a blue and white one, and a yellow and black one.

NOTE: This can be used to tell Finland apart from Sweden, which has many different bus stop signs, most of which have the names of the stops on them.

cards.a: Germany  - Berlin bus stop signs
cards.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.

cards.a: Germany  - Bremen bus stop sign
cards.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.

cards.a: Germany  - Bremerhaven bus stop sign
cards.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section

cards.a: Germany  - Hamburg bus stop signs
cards.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well

cards.a: Germany standard - standard German bus stop signs
cards.note: Like Austria, Germany uses a wide variety of regional bus stops, all of which have the big yellow and green H symbol on them.

cards.a: Ireland (new) - Ireland new bus top signs
cards.note: In the most recent rounds of coverage you’ll find green-and-yellow TFI (Transport for Ireland) bus stop signs, whereas in older coverage you’ll predominantly see Bus Éireann signs.

cards.a: Ireland (old) - Ireland old bus stop signs
cards.note: In the most recent rounds of coverage you’ll find green-and-yellow TFI (Transport for Ireland) bus stop signs, whereas in older coverage you’ll predominantly see Bus Éireann signs.

cards.a: Latvia - Latvia bus stop sign
cards.note:
Latvian bus stop signs have this design.

Most importantly, the bus has five windows. Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia. The other two Baltic countries have four windows.

cards.a: Liechtenstein  - Balzers bus stop sign
cards.note:
Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Balzers sometimes uses black bus stop signs.

NOTE: Regular bus stops are also present.

cards.a: Liechtenstein  - Vaduz bus stop sign
cards.note:
Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Vaduz sometimes uses red bus stop signs.

NOTE: Regular bus stops are also present.

cards.a: Liechtenstein standard - standard Liechtenstein bus stop sign
cards.note:
Bus stops in Liechtenstein use a green-and-white design, with a black metallic border around the sign. The phrase LIEMOBIL is written at the top.

NOTE: The metallic frame is not always black.

cards.a: Lithuania - bus stop sign
cards.note:
Lithuanian bus stop signs have this design.

The bus has four windows. This is mostly useful to distinguish it from the Latvian bus stop sign, which has five windows.

Note however, that Estonia has the same bus stop signs as Lithuania.

cards.a: Luxembourg - bus stop sign
cards.note:
Bus stop signs are blue and always have this exact design. The bus has six windows.

NOTE: Bus stop signs in Belgium and the Netherlands have significantly different designs. For example, the Belgian bus stop sign always has a yellow signpost.

cards.a: Norway - Norway bus stop sign
cards.note:
Norwegian bus stops usually have this small, blue sign with a white bus.

NOTE: Sweden has a lot of different bus stops, none of which look like this.

cards.a: Slovakia (Bratislava) - Bratislava city bus stops
cards.note: For the city of Bratislava, they are different and we find 2 types of stops: The red panels with the blue square but also the numbers of the lines. And in the city center we find rather the blue square and the logo of bus but of face.

cards.note: These bus stops are the most easily recognizable in the country because of their unique shape but BEWARE they are not present everywhere on the 2012 coverage.

cards.a: Switzerland - bus stop signs
cards.note: These bus stop signs, with thick metal signposts going around them, are unique to Switzerland.
